thread:
jamie_support: Hi — customer on 0.9.1 reports ImportError after pip install.
jamie_support: "Traceback (most recent call last):\n  File \"app.py\", line 5, in <module>\n    from redwood import RedwoodClient\nImportError: cannot import name 'RedwoodClient' from 'redwood'"
marta_devex: Did they install with `pip install redwood-inference` or `redwood`? there was a rename a while back.
jamie_support: They ran `pip install redwood-inference==0.9.1` inside a venv. Confirmed package shows as `Name: redwood-inference` in `pip show`.
kevin_eng: Oof, looks like code is still `from redwood import RedwoodClient` which used to be the top-level package. In 0.9.0 we migrated module name to `redwood_inference.client` but kept a shim in previous releases; maybe shim missing in this wheel/sdist scenario.
jamie_support: Customer says reinstalling didn't help. They also have a leftover editable install from local dev (`pip list` shows `redwood @ file:///…/redwood` as an egg-link`).
marta_devex: That egg-link will shadow the installed wheel. Ask them to run `pip uninstall redwood redwood-inference` and check `python -c "import sys; print([p for p in sys.path if 'redwood' in p])"` to find stray paths.
kevin_eng: Also ask them to `python -c "import importlib; print(importlib.import_module('redwood').__file__)"` to see what module is being imported.
jamie_support: Repro steps I sent customer:
1) activate venv
2) `pip uninstall -y redwood redwood-inference`
3) `pip cache purge` (or `pip cache remove` on older pip)
4) `pip install redwood-inference==0.9.1`
5) `python -c "from redwood_inference.client import RedwoodClient; print('ok')"`
They responded with same ImportError after step 4.
kevin_eng: If wheel on PyPI for 0.9.1 was built without the compat shim, importing `redwood` will fail. Check `pip download redwood-inference==0.9.1` and inspect the wheel / .dist-info top-level names.
marta_devex: I pulled the 0.9.1 wheel from our artifact storage — the top-level packages are `redwood_inference` and `redwood` (shim) in the wheel I have. Maybe PyPI upload was partial for some platforms.
jamie_support: Customer is on macOS arm64 (M1). Could be that only sdist was uploaded and build isolation produced different top-level names.
kevin_eng: Ok I'll check our release artifacts and whether the universal wheel was uploaded for arm64. If missing, we should push a 0.9.1.post1 that restores shim and/or update docs.
pip-bot: Release check: 0.9.1 wheel files found: redwood_inference-0.9.1-py3-none-any.whl (x86_64 only), sdist available.
jamie_support: Next steps -> tell customer to install from wheel on x86 emulation as workaround: `pip install --platform=macosx_10_9_x86_64 --only-binary=:all: redwood-inference==0.9.1` or use 0.9.0 for now.
marta_devex: Also add note to release checklist to include macos/arm64 wheel or to ensure shim is included in sdist build step.
kevin_eng: Creating follow-up ticket in releases to push a 0.9.1.post1 and patch release notes.
jamie_support: Customer accepted temporary workaround (install 0.9.0) and asked ETA for fix.
marta_devex: I'll keep them posted. Thanks all :thumbsup:
